For each of the 22 CRC patients receiving anti-PD-1 therapy, the correlation between tumor regression ratio (TRR) and baseline cell subtype proportion was tested using Spearman's rank correlation across patients (one correlation coefficient per cell subtype). The direction of correlation varies by subtype:

POSITIVE correlations (higher baseline proportion → better tumor regression, i.e., greater response):
- CD8 exhausted T cells (c23_CD8_Tex_LAYN): Spearman ρ = +0.506, raw p = 0.016. Pre-existing exhausted CD8 T cells express PD-1 and are the direct cellular target of anti-PD-1 therapy; their presence at baseline provides the substrate for checkpoint blockade to reinvigorate anti-tumor immunity. This is the most mechanistically grounded finding and is consistent with the established biomarker that a T-cell-inflamed tumor microenvironment predicts immunotherapy response (Tumeh et al., Nature 2014; Chen & Mellman, Immunity 2013).
- CD4 regulatory T cells expressing TNFRSF9/CD137 (c13_CD4_Treg_TNFRSF9): ρ = +0.470, p = 0.027. Activated intratumoral Tregs likely serve as a proxy for an overall inflamed, T-cell-rich tumor microenvironment that responds to PD-1 blockade.
- CD4 effector memory RA T cells with granzyme B (c10_CD4_Temra_GZMB): ρ = +0.483, p = 0.023. Cytotoxic CD4 T cells capable of direct tumor killing.
- Vascular smooth muscle cells (c82_SMC_MYH11): ρ = +0.536, p = 0.010 — a low-abundance subset (0.12% mean) with uncertain mechanistic link; may reflect vascular remodeling that facilitates immune infiltration.
- FABP5+ endothelial cells (c68_Endo_FABP5): ρ = +0.502, p = 0.017 — similarly low abundance, may indicate angiogenic remodeling.

NEGATIVE correlations (higher baseline proportion → worse tumor regression, i.e., poorer response):
- Goblet cells (c87_Goblet_MUC2): Spearman ρ = −0.464, raw p = 0.030. MUC2-secreting goblet cells are markers of mucinous colorectal adenocarcinoma. Mucinous histology is a well-established adverse prognostic factor — the extracellular mucin meshwork physically excludes T cells and impairs drug penetration, directly antagonizing anti-PD-1 efficacy (Nitsche et al., Ann Surg Oncol 2013; Luo et al., Cancer Manag Res 2019).
- Normal colonocytes (c84_Coloncyte_CA2): ρ = −0.351, p = 0.110 — trending negative but not statistically significant. May reflect well-differentiated, less immunogenic tumor regions.

CAVEAT: No correlation survived Benjamini-Hochberg FDR correction at q < 0.05 across the 87 tested subtypes (all FDR q ≈ 0.43), reflecting the limited sample size (n=22 patients). All reported associations are exploratory and require independent validation. However, the biological coherence of the top findings — CD8 Tex positively and goblet cells negatively associated with response — supports their plausibility as true signals that a larger cohort could confirm.

IMPLICATION: The baseline tumor microenvironment composition is meaningfully associated with anti-PD-1 response in CRC. An inflamed, T-cell-infiltrated baseline phenotype (enriched for exhausted CD8 T cells and activated CD4 Tregs) correlates with better tumor regression, while a mucinous, goblet-cell-rich phenotype correlates with poorer response. These findings suggest that baseline single-cell profiling can identify patients likely to benefit from checkpoint blockade and highlight mucinous histology as a potential resistance mechanism warranting combination strategies to overcome the physical mucin barrier.
